hidden_points.where: appendix-e.pdf PDF 10 (printed viii, Executive Summary) and PDF 107 (printed 97, Findings)
hidden_points.value: South gap mill could eject at most ~5.8 kg (12.8 lb) of flammable dust; well below mass needed for observed Level-1 damage; therefore combination of ejected dust AND fugitive dust in Level 1 of Mill B was necessary for the initial damaging explosion
hidden_points.quote: the maximum flammable mass of ejected dust when the flame front reaches the exit of the South Gap Mill was approximately 5.8 kg (12.8 lb.). This mass is well below the mass calculated to cause the observed damage ... Therefore, a combination of dust ejected from the South Gap Mill and fugitive dust within level 1 of Mill B was necessary

hidden_points.value: Modelled venting: 11 m2 vent area in Level 1 Mill B keeps walls/doors below failure ('may have mitigated') BUT air shaft remains a path; Multipurpose Building would need ~20% of wall area / 250 m2 vents plus structural continuity. Note: exec summary places the 11 m2 on partition wall + eastern exterior wall, Findings says one vent on southern wall
hidden_points.quote: engineered venting may have mitigated the propagation of the explosion; however, the air shaft would remain a potential path for fire and overpressure ... approximately 20% of the wall surface area, or 250 m2 of total vent area

hidden_points.value: Two methods, two estimates: NFPA 68 -> min cloud 20-30 m3 (2-3% of room) for onset of door damage; CFD -> 40-100 m3 (45-110 lb, 4-10%) most consistent with L1-L2 damage; full-volume cloud -> 82 psi peak (relief via air shaft only). Must keep method attribution; not merge into one number
hidden_points.quote: a minimum cloud volume of approximately 20 to 30 m3 ... between 40 m3 (45 lbs.) and 100 m3 (110 lbs.) of dust ... peak pressure of 82 psi

calculations.expr: 70 m3 x 500 g/m3 = 35,000 g = 35 kg ≈ 77 lb ('roughly 80 lbs')
5.8 kg vs CFD 40-100 m3 ≈ 45-110 lb ≈ 20-50 kg => ejected dust is ~12-29% of the mass needed (≈ 1/8 to 1/3.5)
20-30 m3 vs 40-100 m3: NFPA 68 minimum is for onset of door damage, CFD for L1-L2 damage; not same quantity
Didion 12% of MEC with MEC 60-80 g/m3 implies ≤ ~7-10 g/m3 average in supply duct -> steady-state average, ignores pulse-jet transients (OSHA 2013 critique) and excluded >425 µm
